label: TMUA 2016 · Paper 1 · Question 12

hints.title: Take a central cross-section
hints.body: Let the cylinder radius be r and its half-height be h. In the central cross-section, r, h and the sphere radius 5 form a right triangle.
hints.recap: A central cross-section turns an inscribed-solid condition into a Pythagorean constraint.
hints.pitfall: The right triangle uses the half-height, while the volume uses the full height.

recall.reminder: A central cross-section turns an inscribed-solid condition into a Pythagorean constraint.

hints.title: Make the volume a one-variable expression
hints.body: The constraint is r2+h2=25. The cylinder volume is πr2(2h), so replace r2 using the constraint.
hints.recap: Use a geometric relation to eliminate one unknown before optimising.
hints.pitfall: The largest radius and the largest height cannot occur together.
hints.pause: Write <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow></math> as a polynomial in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow></math> and differentiate.

recall.reminder: Use a geometric relation to eliminate one unknown before optimising.

hints.title: Check that the stationary value is a maximum
hints.body: V=2π(25h−h3) has derivative 2π(25−3h2). The physical interval is 0<h<5.
hints.recap: A derivative changing from positive to negative identifies a maximum.
hints.pitfall: Only the positive stationary half-height is a physical length.
hints.pause: Find that half-height and substitute it into the volume formula.

recall.reminder: A derivative changing from positive to negative identifies a maximum.

solution:
The central cross-section gives r2+h2=25, where h is the half-height. Hence V=πr2(2h)=2πh(25−h2).

dV/dh=2π(25−3h2) vanishes at h=5/3. On 0<h<5, the derivative is positive before this value and negative after it, so it gives the maximum.

The maximum volume is 2π(25−25/3)5/3=5003π/9 cubic centimetres: E.
